items.title: Worked example · Stationary ordered sweeps need not be reversible

source.edition: ASTIS original worked example; scan-order background arXiv:1606.03432v1
source.anchor: Original ASTIS four-state witness; He–De Sa–Mitliagkas–Ré v1 §5 (PDF p. 6), Chen–Štefankovič–Vigoda v4 §1.3 (PDF p. 5), background only
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib example and solution under Apache-2.0. Both linked papers are conceptual background only. No paper wording, figures, or pages redistributed, and the example is not attributed to either source.

items.statement: On the four Boolean pairs, give the equal-bit points mass 3/8 each and the unequal-bit points mass 1/8 each. This is a full-support probability with both marginals uniform. The two displayed Markov kernels are the actual conditional refreshes of the first and second bit respectively. Each is reversible for that same law. The full sweep that performs the first-bit refresh before the second preserves the law but is not reversible.
assumptions: The state space is the finite discrete Boolean pair; all four target masses are specified, not supplied as hypotheses.
The clock advances once per complete sweep: update the first bit given the retained second bit, then update the second given the new first bit. Composition order is fixed.

formulae.label: The full sweep preserves the law but violates detailed balance

obligations.label: Prove the conditional refresh laws, reversible factors, sweep invariance, and the exact counterexample to sweep reversibility.

bindings.boundary: An original full-support four-state witness at sweep time. No statement about all systematic scans, the per-update process with an alternating rule, scan-position augmentation, mixing time, or a paper theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: Original four-state full-support probability with the exact two conditional updates in order.
assumption_deltas.lean: An explicitly weighted finite sum of Dirac measures, actual countable-domain kernels, and Q ∘ₖ P in Mathlib's second-after-first convention.
assumption_deltas.reason: The theorem proves all row and target masses and both conditional laws. The literal state and kernels are let-bound with no extra input hypothesis.

assumption_deltas.source: Detailed balance and invariance of the actual kernels.
assumption_deltas.lean: Set-lintegral Kernel.IsReversible and measure equality Kernel.Invariant, with singleton fluxes used to refute the former.
assumption_deltas.reason: All singleton subsets are measurable; the positive-mass witness rules out reversibility under the actual definition. No domain or mixing conclusion is added.
